- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 1.0) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–7 days.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -1.5), model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–4% for next 3–5 days.  
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 1–2 days); cap forecast peak at 2–3 standard deviations above recent mean.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion after a spike, model often fails to correct; apply downward bias of 2–5% for 3–7 days post-spike.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to underestimate in periods of high volatility; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast if sentiment shows rising volatility or recent sharp moves.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– swings (e.g., +1.1, -1.4, +1.2), model often misreads trend direction; favor midpoint of sentiment range for 5–10 day horizon.
